envelope.text: THE BOUND, for a backend that cannot assign ids only

why:
issue 2009 (2026-10-23) -- KEYED. `rclcpp::PollClient<S>::remove_pending_request(Future&)` now erases the request keyed by its SEQUENCE NUMBER, as upstream erases its map entry: the future leaves the client's pending list (`rclcpp::detail::PendingList`), so a reply that arrives later is DROPPED -- it used to be taken by the next future the same client handed out. It still answers true iff the future was a pending request of THIS client (another client's future answers false and stays pending) and false on a second call. Divergence because the verb lives on the poll client, not on `rclcpp::Client` (the dispatch half, `cpp:PollClient`). THE BOUND, written on the declaration, is now confined to a backend that cannot assign ids (`NROS_RMW_SEQUENCE_ID_UNKNOWN`; no in-tree backend): there a late reply cannot say whose it is, so the next unkeyed reply is dropped in its place rather than delivered to a newer request. Held by `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/client_seq_correlation_runtime.cpp` (a removed request's late reply is staged and the next future does not receive it).

Previous text (issue 1996): "RE-VERDICTED declined -> divergence/adopt-bounded ... THE BOUND: upstream erases a map entry keyed by the sequence number, so a reply arriving later is DROPPED; ours has one request in flight and no key, so a reply arriving after removal is still taken by the next future the same client hands out." That bound is gone.

issue 2037 (2026-10-25) -- upstream's three overloads are reachable on the poll client: `remove_pending_request(FutureAndRequestId&)` (what `async_send_request` returns), `remove_pending_request(int64_t request_id)` (`PendingList::remove_seq`: the future waiting on that id becomes invalid and its late reply is dropped; false for an id with no pending request), and, with `std::promise`, `remove_pending_request(const SharedFutureAndRequestId&)`, after which every copy settles to a null response. Held by `client_future_and_request_id_runtime.cpp`.
